evidenceClaims.statement: A deep or indeterminate extremity soft-tissue mass should have local MRI characterization and specialist planning before tissue sampling.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Ultrasound remains useful for initial triage. No universal limb-wide field, size threshold or histologic diagnosis from MRI is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: An exported image subset and the complete original MRI examination are different evidence objects; a report of additional acquired series warrants reconciliation with the imaging service before deciding that a new examination is required.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The retrieve-versus-repeat application is an explicitly identified clinical/editorial inference from examination comparability and local staging requirements. No guideline mandates the exact administrative workflow; original files must actually be retrievable.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Image-guided core biopsy planned with the definitive-treatment team is the preferred initial tissue approach for a suspicious deep soft-tissue mass.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Incisional biopsy can be appropriate after nondiagnostic cores or when core sampling is unsafe. Small superficial excision exceptions do not apply to the constructed deep masses.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: The biopsy tract should be selected so that it can be included safely in the definitive sarcoma resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Constructed corridors still require sarcoma/radiology anatomical confirmation. Tract planning must not become a reason to omit necessary pre-treatment diagnosis.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: A sample containing tissue outside the imaged lesion does not establish the histology of that unsampled lesion; unresolved radiology-pathology mismatch requires representative tissue assessment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Specific repeat-targeted-core versus open-biopsy ranking is an application to a documented off-target sample and a feasible corrected percutaneous route, not a universal repeat-core count.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Intermediate- or high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma requires chest CT staging before definitive treatment even if an initial chest radiograph is unrevealing.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Other staging depends on subtype and site. This statement does not rank every low-risk lesion or frail-patient pathway.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: FDG PET/CT is not the routine replacement for conventional local imaging and chest CT staging in ordinary adult-type soft-tissue sarcoma.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Selected histologies, diagnostic problems and radical surgery planning may justify PET.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Perioperative radiotherapy improves local control in higher-risk extremity sarcoma and can accompany limb-preserving surgery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not a claim of improved overall survival or universal need in all low-grade/superficial tumors.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Preoperative extremity radiotherapy generally uses a smaller volume with less late fibrosis, while postoperative radiotherapy has fewer acute wound problems but more late morbidity.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Local control is broadly comparable; exact sequence remains an MDT decision. No dose, timing interval or complication percentage is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Early surgery followed by postoperative radiotherapy can be appropriate for a rapidly growing painful resectable limb sarcoma or when preoperative wound risk is a major concern.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly adequate guideline for this patient-specific sequencing boundary; SEOM independently corroborates the wound/late-toxicity tradeoff, not a deterministic patient-selection rule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: A margin must be interpreted using tumor at ink, the anatomical barrier, subtype, prior therapy and whether the boundary was planned at a critical structure.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No universal centimeter rule is applied. A close negative critical-structure margin is not equivalent to an inadvertent multifocal positive margin.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: An additional postoperative radiation boost after preoperative radiotherapy is not routinely supported merely because a sarcoma margin is close or microscopically positive.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One adequate direct guideline; this does not bar individualized additional therapy for gross residual disease or establish that every R1 margin may be observed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: After unplanned sarcoma excision with positive margins, staging and surgical-bed MRI are required; re-excision may still be indicated with no visible residual tumor if clearance is feasible with acceptable morbidity.
evidenceClaims.limitation: MRI cannot exclude microscopic residual disease. Re-excision is not mandatory when morbidity is prohibitive or adequate bed clearance cannot be achieved.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Suspected primary retroperitoneal sarcoma is usually diagnosed through specialist-planned percutaneous coaxial core biopsy rather than FNA or open/laparoscopic biopsy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Expert-pathognomonic liposarcoma with no preoperative treatment may be an exception; this is not the constructed indeterminate solid mass. No needle gauge or seeding rate is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Localized resectable retroperitoneal sarcoma should be removed as an intact macroscopically complete specimen, with involved contiguous structures managed according to histotype and anatomy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not all adjacent normal organs need removal for every subtype; feasibility requires a specialist high-volume team.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: For retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma, resection includes involved structures while adjacent uninvolved organs can be preserved; the wider ipsilateral approach considered for liposarcoma should not be applied automatically.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One direct adequate guideline for the histotype-specific distinction; SEOM corroborates intact en bloc surgery generally. Reconstructed vascular anatomy remains a clinician-review requirement.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Radiotherapy is not routine for all resectable retroperitoneal sarcoma, and evidence does not support applying the extremity high-grade preoperative-radiation rule to retroperitoneal leiomyosarcoma.
evidenceClaims.limitation: BSG discusses possible benefit in selected low/intermediate-grade liposarcoma; SEOM emphasizes the negative overall trial. This packet withholds a universal low-grade-liposarcoma radiation key.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Desmoid tumors can be locally infiltrative and recurrent but do not have metastatic potential.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Local morbidity can still be substantial; nonmetastatic does not mean harmless or exempt from treatment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Specialist active surveillance is an appropriate initial/continuing strategy for desmoid disease with stable observations, limited symptoms and no threat to meaningful function or critical structures.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Serial growth, worsening function and critical-site threat change the decision; no fixed scan interval is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Persistent desmoid growth with clinically important worsening symptoms or threatened function warrants renewed active-treatment planning rather than indefinite surveillance.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Treatment is selected by site, disease tempo, morbidity and patient goals; a single measurement does not define a universal threshold.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Function-preserving surgery can be offered for selected progressing symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid after surveillance when resection morbidity is acceptable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Surgery is an option, not universally superior to every systemic/local alternative or mandatory for every desmoid.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: A microscopic margin can be accepted in desmoid surgery to avoid functional or cosmetic harm; the finding does not automatically require wider re-excision or adjuvant radiation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly adequate current guideline for the margin boundary. Postoperative RT evidence is limited; absence of gross disease and stable/improving function are essential to the constructed follow-up.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: A mesenteric/abdominal desmoid, absent tumor CTNNB1 mutation and a polyposis family history raise concern for APC-associated disease and warrant colorectal/genetic evaluation.
evidenceClaims.limitation: BSG directly lists the risk features and colonoscopy/APC investigation; SEOM corroborates the FAP/desmoid association. No inherited diagnosis is proven by a negative tumor test.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Medical treatment is generally preferred to morbid resection for progressive desmoid outside the favorable abdominal-wall setting.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Urgent obstruction/ischemia or another immediate surgical complication requires separate assessment; neither is present in the constructed ambulatory chart review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Nirogacestat is an FDA-approved systemic option for adults with progressing desmoid who require systemic treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No superiority to sorafenib, dosing, mandatory line of therapy or automatic choice for a specific fertility goal is claimed. Ovarian toxicity and other adverse effects require counseling.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: MRI and a bland fatty core may not resolve a deep lipomatous lesion; MDM2 amplification testing can distinguish ALT/well-differentiated liposarcoma from a lipoma.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One direct adequate current guideline. Sampling and expert pathology remain important; MDM2 does not by itself grade the unsampled whole lesion or prove dedifferentiation.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: For a symptomatic extremity ALT without dedifferentiation, complete marginal en bloc resection preserving major neurovascular structures can be appropriate instead of a wide function-sacrificing sarcoma resection.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One direct adequate current guideline. This favorable extremity behavior should not be generalized to retroperitoneal liposarcoma or dedifferentiated disease.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Single-agent doxorubicin is a standard first-line option for advanced adult-type soft-tissue sarcoma; adding ifosfamide is principally considered when greater shrinkage is clinically important, with greater toxicity.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Histology and goals matter. This does not make every patient eligible for anthracyclines, prescribe a dose or rank options after prior therapy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the constructed topic cases; observations are fictional, not empirical outcome data.

evidenceClaims.statement: Planned sarcoma biopsy should avoid contaminating a separate unaffected compartment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The exact compartment rule is directly checked in older ESSR technique guidance; current SEOM corroborates tract removal/planning. Constructed rectus/adductor and triceps/biceps paths require clinician anatomy review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified adult synthetic teaching cases; constructed observations are not observed patient data.
evidenceClaims.reuseMode: Exact existing claim reused; no fresh technical-guide retrieval.

evidenceClaims.statement: Some sarcoma histologies, including alveolar soft part and clear cell sarcoma, justify brain staging; that indication should not be generalized to ordinary extremity UPS.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No universal brain-imaging schedule or diagnostic sensitivity is claimed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated differential or management setting in original constructed topic cases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Concern for APC-associated polyposis calls for direct colorectal/endoscopic and genetic evaluation; an occult-blood screening test does not characterize adenoma burden.
evidenceClaims.limitation: The FIT comparison is an application of the diagnostic goal, not a trial-derived FIT sensitivity or universal screening-age rule.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated differential or management setting in original constructed topic cases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Sorafenib is an active systemic option for selected progressing desmoid disease rather than a requirement for stable improving disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No superiority over nirogacestat, dose, availability or mandatory sequence is claimed.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated differential or management setting in original constructed topic cases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Tumor CTNNB1 analysis can support a desmoid workup; it does not resolve an otherwise lipomatous lesion as ALT versus lipoma.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One adequate guideline for desmoid/ALT molecular distinctions; morphology and representative tissue remain essential.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated differential or management setting in original constructed topic cases.

evidenceClaims.statement: SS18 rearrangement assessment addresses a synovial-sarcoma differential.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Targeted molecular association only; no claim that every SS18 finding is diagnostic irrespective of fusion partner and morphology.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated differential or management setting in original constructed topic cases.

evidenceClaims.statement: Assessment of contrast-related signal change in an intrinsically bright soft-tissue mass region requires accounting for acquisition settings; a pre/post comparison that also changes suppression cannot simply assign all signal differences to enhancement.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Technical application of previously verified primary MRI characterization/contrast-targeting guidance, reused offline. Only one adequate medical primary consensus source is mapped; no new direct verification of the exact constructed sequence pair occurred. MSK radiology must confirm this comparison and its priority. No universal sequence mandate, contrast dose, numerical enhancement criterion, tract or histologic diagnosis is inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The identified named synthetic adult teaching cases; measurements and acquisition observations are constructed, not empirical patient/gameplay data.
evidenceClaims.reuseMode: Exact local inference retained; original lastCheckedOn preserved.

evidenceClaims.statement: Absent FDG uptake does not establish that a small pulmonary nodule is benign in sarcoma; pulmonary CT remains necessary and CT morphology alone may still leave a nodule indeterminate.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No nodule-size risk threshold, metastatic probability, automatic biopsy indication or follow-up interval is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: Core sampling of a heterogeneous retroperitoneal mass should address solid enhancing areas that may contain a higher-grade component; sampling a fatty part alone can underrepresent the lesion.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Exact corridors require specialist review. A suspected solid component is not itself proof of dedifferentiation.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: MDM2 amplification can support the well-differentiated/dedifferentiated liposarcoma family but does not determine the grade or histology of an unsampled component.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Molecular/pathology facts inform the lipomatous differential across sites; retroperitoneal surgical policy is not transferred to the extremity. Representative histology is still required.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: Intersecting atypical spindle-cell fascicles with myoid-marker expression support a smooth-muscle sarcoma differential; MDM2, GIST and melanocytic markers help distinguish mimics in a retroperitoneal tumor.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One directly adequate professional recommendation for this constructed panel. The combination is not a universally sufficient stain-only diagnosis; expert pathology must confirm the exact teaching application.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: After complete gross retroperitoneal sarcoma resection, routine adjuvant external-beam radiation or chemotherapy has no proven benefit; postoperative radiation is especially constrained by gastrointestinal toxicity.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Selected focal residual-risk situations require expert review; this is not a blanket ban on all radiotherapy or trials. Constructed diffuse microscopic margins and no defined target are essential to this example.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: A prior enlargement followed by current stability and recovery of usual function should not be described as ongoing persistent progression solely because the mass remains larger than baseline.
evidenceClaims.limitation: An explicit application of persistent clinical/radiologic progression and symptom-based surveillance boundaries, not a new growth cutoff or mandatory waiting interval. Exact longitudinal case requires clinician review.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: A normal distal colorectal examination does not assess the proximal colon; complete colonoscopy is important when evaluating possible APC-associated polyposis, including phenotypes with proximal adenomas.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No screening age or interval is authored. The abnormal family/tumor pattern raises evaluation, not a proven inherited diagnosis.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: For progressive desmoid outside the favorable abdominal-wall setting, systemic therapy is a standard pathway; radiotherapy has selected roles and is not automatically preferred before medical treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No systemic-agent superiority is claimed. SEOM directly places RT among options when surgery is unsuitable and medical treatment fails; this is not a universal prohibition on initial local therapy.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The stated original constructed adult scenarios; patient measurements and records are fictional, not empirical probabilities.

evidenceClaims.statement: Pazopanib has selected first-line roles in some older STS patients, while gemcitabine/docetaxel is not the routine first-line substitute for doxorubicin in an anthracycline-eligible adult-type STS patient.
evidenceClaims.limitation: One adequate current society guideline for the alternative-regimen roles. No direct pazopanib-versus-doxorubicin/ifosfamide superiority claim or age cutoff is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: The exact constructed first-line metastatic UPS scenario; other histologies and contraindications differ.
